hook.situation: A friend asks, '어제 뭐 했어요?' If you answer in present tense — 영화 봐요, 밥 먹어요 — it sounds like you are talking about your usual routine or what you do now. For yesterday, Korean needs the polite past frame: 봤어요, 먹었어요, 갔어요, 했어요.
objectives: Choose 았어요 vs 었어요 from the last vowel of the stem
Handle the first everyday contractions and irregulars: 했어요, 봤어요, 왔어요, 추웠어요
hook.whyItMatters: Past tense is the grammar that lets beginners tell real stories. You use it after class, on KakaoTalk, when explaining why you are late, and any time someone asks what happened. A clean short past sentence sounds much more natural than a long sentence with the wrong tense.

grammarNotes.title: V았/었어요 — the polite past tense
grammarNotes.func: Use V았/었어요 to say an action or state happened in the past. It is the polite, everyday way to answer questions like "What did you do yesterday?"

formTable.when: Stem's last vowel is ㅏ or ㅗ
formTable.ex: 가다 → 갔어요, 보다 → 봤어요, 살다 → 살았어요

formTable.when: Any other vowel (ㅓ, ㅜ, ㅣ, ㅡ, ㅔ …)
formTable.ex: 먹다 → 먹었어요, 마시다 → 마셨어요, 읽다 → 읽었어요
하다 → 했어요, 공부하다 → 공부했어요, 일하다 → 일했어요

examples.note: 만나다's stem 만나- ends in ㅏ, so -았 contracts: 만나 + 았 → 만났어요.

examples.en: I ate (a meal) in the morning.
examples.note: 먹- has the vowel ㅓ, so it takes -었어요 (no contraction).

examples.en: I studied Korean at home yesterday.
examples.note: 공부하다 is a 하다 verb, so 하다 → 했어요 → 공부했어요.

examples.en: I watched a movie over the weekend.
examples.note: 보다's stem 보- ends in ㅗ, so 보 + 았 → 봤어요.

keyPoint.label: 이다 → 였어요 / 이었어요
keyPoint.body: The copula 이다 ("to be") has its own past form. After a vowel use 였어요 (친구이다 → 친구였어요), and after a final consonant use 이었어요 (학생이다 → 학생이었어요; 책이다 → 책이었어요). For now just memorize these two endings — the full ins and outs of 이다 come in its home chapter.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 먹었어요 links across the boundary and sounds like [머거써요]; 했어요 sounds like [해써요] — the 어 is swallowed and the ㅆ is tense.

drill.instruction: Change each verb into the polite past form V았/었어요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English often leans on the time word ("yesterday") and leaves the verb in its plain form. In Korean the verb itself has to carry the past tense — adding 어제 (yesterday) does not make 가요 mean "went." You have to change 가요 to 갔어요.

exampleSentence.note: 어제 almost always pulls the sentence into past tense.

exampleSentence.en: I went to Busan last week.
exampleSentence.note: 지난주에 marks when the completed event happened.

exampleSentence.en: I came to Korea last year.
exampleSentence.note: 오다 becomes 왔어요 in the past.

exampleSentence.en: I ate dinner at a restaurant.
I watched a movie with a friend.
I went to Busan last week.
I went to a cafe with a friend.
exampleSentence.note: 친구랑 is natural in casual polite conversation.

exampleSentence.en: The movie was a little long.
exampleSentence.note: Adjectives also take past tense: 길다 → 길었어요.
Use 에서 for where the action happened.

extendedDialogue.setting: Two friends talk about yesterday after class.

lines.grammarNote: 했어요 is the polite past form of 하다.

lines.ko: 친구랑 영화를 봤어요. 그다음에 식당에서 밥을 먹었어요.
lines.romanization: chingurang yeonghwareul bwasseoyo. geudaeume sikdangeseo babeul meogeosseoyo.
lines.en: I watched a movie with a friend. After that, we ate at a restaurant.
lines.grammarNote: 봤어요 and 먹었어요 are two finished events in sequence.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.grammarNote: 어땠어요 asks for a past evaluation.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: It was a little long, but it was fun.
lines.grammarNote: 길었지만 and 재미있었어요 show past adjectives plus contrast.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: About what time did you come home?
lines.grammarNote: 왔어요 is the contracted past of 오다.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 열한 시쯤 왔어요. 날씨가 추워서 바로 잤어요.

lines.en: I came home around eleven. It was cold, so I went straight to sleep.
lines.grammarNote: 왔어요 and 잤어요 are past actions; 추워서 gives the reason.

readingText.title: 어제 한 일
readingText.body: 어제는 수업이 끝난 뒤에 친구를 만났어요. 같이 카페에 갔고, 저는 커피를 마셨어요. 친구는 차를 마셨어요. 그다음 영화를 봤어요. 영화는 조금 길었지만 마지막 장면이 정말 재미있었어요. 집에 올 때는 날씨가 추웠어요. 그래서 집에 오자마자 따뜻한 물을 마시고 바로 잤어요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Yesterday, after class ended, I met a friend. We went to a cafe together, and I drank coffee. My friend drank tea. Then we watched a movie. The movie was a little long, but the last scene was really fun. When I came home, the weather was cold. So as soon as I got home, I drank warm water and went straight to sleep.

comprehensionQuestions.question: What did the writer do after class?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 친구를 만났어요 and 같이 카페에 갔어요.

comprehensionQuestions.question: Find three contracted past forms in the text.
Which adjective uses the ㅂ irregular past form?

culturalNote.title: Short Past Answers Sound Natural
culturalNote.body: When Koreans ask 어제 뭐 했어요?, they are often opening a small everyday conversation, not asking for a long report. A natural answer can be short: 친구 만났어요, 영화 봤어요, 집에서 쉬었어요. Once the tense is clean, you can add one detail: 누구랑, 어디에서, 어땠는지. Accurate short past sentences are better than long translated sentences with the wrong ending.
culturalNote.tip: Answer in one finished event first, then add time, person, or place.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence correctly reports a completed action yesterday?
inlineExercises.explanation: 봤어요 is the polite past form, so it fits 어제.
먹다 uses -었어요 in the past: 먹었어요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: 어제 날씨가 춥었어요.
inlineExercises.explanation: 춥다 is a ㅂ irregular adjective. In the past it becomes 추웠어요, not 춥었어요.

options: how something was in the past
inlineExercises.correct: how something was in the past
inlineExercises.explanation: 어땠어요 is the past form of 어떻다.

inlineExercises.hint: 오다 becomes 왔어요 in the past.
inlineExercises.explanation: 집에 왔어요 is the natural way to say you came home. 늦게 describes how the coming happened, so it goes before 왔어요.

inlineExercises.prompt: 친구___ 영화를 봤어요. (I watched a movie with a friend.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 친구랑 means with a friend. 를 would make the friend the thing watched, and 에 would mark a place or direction.
보다 contracts in past polite form: 보았어요 becomes 봤어요. 어제 makes the past tense necessary.
어제 sets the past time, and 만났어요 marks the completed meeting. 친구 is the person met, so 친구를 comes before the verb.
어제 is a past-time word, so the verb must be past tense. 가요 becomes 갔어요.

bullets: Past snapshot: use -았/었어요 for finished events.
ㅏ/ㅗ usually take -았어요; most other vowels take -었어요.
Memorize the high-frequency contractions: 했어요, 갔어요, 왔어요, 봤어요.

writingTask.prompt: Answer the question "What did you do yesterday?" in 3 sentences about where you went, who you met, and what you ate.
writingTask.hint: Use V았/었어요 for every verb (갔어요, 만났어요, 먹었어요).
writingTask.model: 어제 친구를 만났어요. 같이 영화를 봤어요. 그리고 식당에서 밥을 먹었어요.
writingTask.modelEn: Yesterday I met a friend. We watched a movie together. And we ate at a restaurant.

canDo: Say a past action with the polite past tense V았/었어요 (먹었어요 · 갔어요)
Answer "what did you do yesterday?" in one clean sentence (어제 …었어요)
Conjugate the past tense correctly by vowel harmony (만났어요 · 봤어요 · 했어요)
Place a past time word at the start (어제 · 지난주 · 작년)
